newsitem.title: USA: TIG shares down after Q1, growth outlook.
newsitem.headline: TIG shares down after Q1, growth outlook.

text.p: Shares of TIG Holdings Inc fell sharply after the company reported disappointing first quarter earnings and warned about the outlook for earnings growth.
TIG reported first quarter operating earnings of $0.62 a share compared with the First Call consensus estimate of $0.68 a share. TIG shares fell 2-7/8 to 28-1/2.
TIG Holdings Inc chief executive Jon Rotenstreich said the company's first quarter results were hurt by non-catastrophe property losses in its retail and commercial specialty divisions.
"We are in the process of refining our retail business strategy to reduce the exposure to and the impact from these types of losses," Rotenstreich said in a statement.
In addition, he said, competitive market conditions in the commercial insurance and reinsurance industry have encouraged TIG to remain selective in its underwriting process.
"We do not anticipate any change in pricing conditions during 1997, therefore these conditions could moderate earnings growth until our recent initiatives reach full production," he said.

TIG president Don Hutson said the company will continue to emphasize capital management, noting that over the past three years, the company has repurchased nearly 19 percent of its shares outstanding.
In the first quarter of 1997, the company repurchased 1.4 million shares of its common stock at an average price of $35.09 per common share as part of its ongoing stock repurchase program.

To date, TIG Holdings has repurchased 12.1 million shares of its common stock at an average price of $27.89 per common share, or 18.9 percent of the common shares outstanding at the time of the program's inception in 1994.
Although the company's earnings fell short of expectations, the combined ratio showed marked improvement.
The combined ratio fell to 102.7 percent in the first quarter from 111.3 percent a year ago.
The combined ratio indicates whether or not a company is earnings a profit on the business it writes. An underwriting profit occurs when the ratio is below 100 percent.
TIG shares extended their fall by late morning, dropping 3-1/2 or more than 11 percent, to 27-7/8.
